cards.text: Grab your apron, friend: after the Levites, Chronicles keeps listing Israel's families tribe by tribe, and Issachar is up first. Issachar has four sons, and Tola's sons head their families. In the days of David, Tola's descendants number 22,600 mighty men of valor, and Issachar's families total 87,000.
Benjamin's three sons come next. Each one has a line of family heads and thousands of mighty men of valor fit for battle.
Then Naphtali's four sons get a quick mention, the descendants of Bilhah, Rachel's servant (Genesis 30:3-8).
Then comes Manasseh's family, through Machir, the father of Gilead. One descendant, a man named Zelophehad, has only daughters.
Next up is Ephraim, Joseph's son (Genesis 41:52), with a line of sons. Then the list stops cold: Ezer and Elead are killed by the natives of Gath, a Philistine city (1 Samuel 6:17).

cards.question: Ephraim's sons Ezer and Elead are killed by the natives of Gath. What does the text say they had gone down to do?

answers.text: Spy out the city of Gath

cards.question: After Ezer and Elead die, true or false: their father Ephraim mourns for many days.
Later, Ephraim's wife gives birth to another son. Ephraim names him Beriah, because ___ had come upon his house.
Sheerah, a daughter in Ephraim's family, gets a line all her own. What does she do?

cards.text: Ephraim's line runs on, son after son, down to Nun and his son JOSHUA, the man God called to lead Israel after Moses died (Joshua 1:1-2). Finding Joshua in this list is like digging through a junk drawer and finding the good scissors. Joseph's descendants live in towns like Bethel, Shechem, Gezer and Megiddo.

Then comes Asher: sons, a couple of sisters, and family after family, called choice and mighty men of valor, with 26,000 fit for battle. Choice and mighty! The nicest thing anybody ever wrote on me was a price sticker that said 25 cents.

Then the list circles back to Benjamin for a closer look. Some heads of families living in Geba are carried into exile, and a man named Shaharaim has sons in Moab. Two more of his sons are Abitub and Elpaal.

cards.question: Elpaal's son Shemed leaves his mark on the map. True or false: Shemed tears down the towns of Ono and Lod.
Two more of Elpaal's sons, Beriah and Shema, head families living in Aijalon. What do they do to the people of Gath?

cards.text: Then come the sons of Beriah, Elpaal, Shimei, Shashak and Jeroham, name after name. And that's a different Beriah than Ephraim's son, like two guys named Mike in the same group chat. All these heads of families live in Jerusalem.
Then comes Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, who lives in Gibeon with his wife Maacah and their sons. The text says they too live alongside their relatives in Jerusalem.

Then the list lands on a name you'll know: Kish's son Saul, who became Israel's king (1 Samuel 11:15). His sons are Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab and Esh-baal, and Jonathan's line runs down through Merib-baal and Micah to Azel and Azel's brother Eshek. Eshek's son Ulam has sons who are mighty men of valor and archers, with many sons and grandsons, 150 in all. All these are descendants of Benjamin.
